issues.title: Phase 1: Establish Context
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 1: Establish Context

Before any technical controls are implemented, the organization must understand *why* it is subject to NIST 800-171 R3 and *what* needs to be protected.

---

### Sub-components

**1a - Define Statutory and Regulatory Obligations**
- Identify all contracts containing DFARS 252.204-7012, -7019, -7020, -7021
- Identify applicable CMMC Level requirements (Level 1, 2, or 3)
- Document the specific DoD program(s) driving the requirement
- Confirm whether a C3PAO assessment or self-assessment applies

**1b - Define CUI and FCI**
- Identify specific CUI categories that apply (use NIST SP 800-171 and the CUI Registry)
- Define what Federal Contract Information (FCI) the organization handles
- Document CUI handling requirements for each identified category
- Confirm which CUI categories are in scope for CMMC

**1c - Identify Your PPTDF (People, Processes, Technology, Data, Facilities)**
- People: staff, contractors, third parties who touch CUI/FCI
- Processes: business processes that create, receive, store, or transmit CUI/FCI
- Technology: systems, software, and services involved in CUI/FCI handling
- Data: all CUI/FCI data types, formats, and locations
- Facilities: physical locations where CUI/FCI is processed or stored

**1d - Develop a Resource Plan**
- Estimate budget for compliance implementation (tools, labor, consultants)
- Identify internal owners for each Kill Chain phase
- Define the project timeline working backward from the C3PAO assessment date
- Obtain executive sponsorship and sign-off

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All contracts requiring CMMC/171 compliance identified and documented
- [ ] CUI categories defined and mapped to NIST 800-171 R3 requirements
- [ ] PPTDF inventory documented
- [ ] Resource plan approved by executive leadership
- [ ] POA&M items for gaps identified in this phase created

---

### NIST 800-171 R3 Controls Addressed
This phase is foundational - it does not map to specific controls but enables accurate scoping for all 97 core CUI controls.

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 1 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 2: Implement Governance
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 2: Implement Governance

Governance is the backbone of a defensible compliance program. Without documented policies and standards, technical controls have no authoritative basis.

---

### Sub-components

**2a - Develop Policies and Standards**
- Create or update an Information Security Policy aligned to NIST 800-171 R3 control families
- Develop standards for each control domain (AC, AT, AU, CM, IA, IR, MA, MP, PE, RA, CA, SC, SI)
- Ensure policies address all 97 core CUI controls
- Incorporate DoD-specified Organization Defined Parameters (ODPs) into policy language
  - Example: 90-day account inactivity threshold (03.01.01.f.02)
  - Example: 24-hour notification for account changes (03.01.01.g.01-.03)
  - Example: 16-character minimum passwords (per DoD ODP)
  - Example: Quarterly vulnerability scanning frequency
- Obtain policy approval from executive leadership
- Distribute policies to all personnel

**2b - Prioritize PPTDF for Compliance**
- Using the PPTDF inventory from Phase 1, rank components by risk and compliance impact
- Assign control owners to each PPTDF element
- Document the prioritization rationale in the SSP or governance document

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Information Security Policy approved and published
- [ ] Standards created for all 17 NIST 800-171 R3 control families
- [ ] DoD ODPs incorporated into policy language
- [ ] Control owners assigned for all 97 core CUI controls
- [ ] PPTDF prioritization documented
- [ ] POA&M items for policy gaps created

---

### NIST 800-171 R3 Controls Addressed
All control families - governance documents provide the authoritative basis for implementation of all 287 discrete requirements.

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 2 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 3: Establish Compliance Scope
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 3: Establish Compliance Scope

Accurate scoping is essential. Over-scoping wastes resources; under-scoping creates compliance gaps. This phase produces the core documentation artifacts that define the assessment boundary.

---

### Sub-components

**3a - Data Flow Diagram (DFD)**
- Map all data flows involving CUI/FCI
- Show where CUI enters, is processed, stored, and exits the environment
- Identify all internal systems and external connections in the CUI flow
- Document encryption status at each flow point

**3b - Asset Inventory**
- Enumerate all hardware assets in scope (workstations, servers, network devices, mobile)
- Enumerate all software assets (applications, OS, middleware, databases)
- Tag each asset as in-scope, out-of-scope, or CUI-adjacent
- Include cloud assets and virtual infrastructure

**3c - Network Diagram**
- Create a current-state network topology diagram
- Show segmentation between CUI environment and other networks
- Identify all ingress/egress points
- Document firewall rules and access control points relevant to CUI

**3d - External Service Provider (ESP) Inventory**
- List all third-party services that process, store, or transmit CUI on behalf of the org
- Assess each ESP for CMMC/FIPS compliance (cloud providers, MSPs, SaaS)
- Document FedRAMP authorization status for cloud services
- Obtain CMMC self-attestation or C3PAO certs from relevant ESPs

**3e - Roles and Responsibilities**
- Define all roles that interact with CUI/FCI systems
- Document access privileges associated with each role
- Establish a separation of duties matrix
- Map roles to NIST 800-171 R3 control requirements (03.01.04)

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] DFD reviewed and approved; reflects current state
- [ ] Asset inventory complete and under configuration control
- [ ] Network diagram current and reviewed by security team
- [ ] All ESPs inventoried; compliance status documented for each
- [ ] Roles and responsibilities matrix complete; separation of duties validated
- [ ] All documents incorporated into SSP

---

### NIST 800-171 R3 Controls Addressed
03.01.03 (Information Flow Enforcement), 03.01.04 (Separation of Duties), 03.04.01 (Baseline Configuration), 03.16.01-03.16.02 (Planning)

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 3 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 4: Risk Management
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 4: Risk Management

A mature risk management program is required by NIST 800-171 R3. This phase ensures risks are identified, assessed, and managed systematically rather than reactively.

---

### Sub-components

**4a - Risk Management Plan (RMP)**
- Document the organization's risk management methodology
- Define risk acceptance criteria and risk appetite
- Establish risk assessment frequency (DoD ODP requires periodic assessment)
- Identify risk owners for each identified risk

**4b - Cyber Supply Chain Risk Management (C-SCRM) Plan**
- Identify all suppliers and third parties in the CUI supply chain
- Assess supply chain risks for each critical supplier
- Document acquisition security requirements (hardware/software sourcing)
- Address counterfeit component risks
- Reference NIST SP 800-161r1 for C-SCRM guidance

**4c - Acquisition Strategies**
- Incorporate security requirements into procurement processes
- Include CMMC flow-down clauses in subcontractor agreements
- Establish vendor security assessment process prior to onboarding
- Document acceptable use and data handling requirements in contracts

**4d - Enforce SCRM**
- Implement controls to monitor supplier compliance
- Establish processes to respond to supply chain incidents
- Conduct periodic supplier security reviews

**4e - Weakness / Vulnerability Process**
- Define the process for identifying, tracking, and remediating weaknesses
- Establish vulnerability scanning cadence (DoD ODP: quarterly minimum)
- Link vulnerability findings to POA&M
- Define remediation SLAs by severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low)

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Risk Management Plan documented and approved
- [ ] C-SCRM Plan documented covering all critical suppliers
- [ ] Acquisition security requirements embedded in procurement process
- [ ] SCRM monitoring process operational
- [ ] Vulnerability management process documented with SLAs defined
- [ ] Initial risk assessment complete; risks entered in risk register

---

### NIST 800-171 R3 Controls Addressed
03.11.01-03.11.03 (Risk Assessment), 03.14.01-03.14.07 (System and Information Integrity - vulnerability scanning), 03.16.03 (Supply Chain Risk Management)

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 4 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 5: Document CUI/FCI Environment
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 5: Document CUI/FCI Environment

Formal documentation of the CUI environment is required for both the C3PAO assessment and ongoing compliance maintenance. The SSP is the primary artifact assessed during CMMC.

---

### Sub-components

**5a - System Security Plan (SSP)**
- Document all 97 NIST 800-171 R3 core CUI controls and their implementation status
- For each control, describe: what is in place, who is responsible, and how compliance is demonstrated
- Include all Phase 1-4 artifacts by reference (DFD, network diagram, asset inventory, RMP)
- Address all 287 discrete requirements (Assessment Objectives)
- Incorporate DoD ODP values throughout
- Document Inherited controls (from FedRAMP-authorized cloud providers where applicable)
- Keep SSP under version control; establish review/update cadence

**5b - Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&M)**
- Document all known gaps identified during gap assessment
- For each gap: control ID, description, risk level, responsible party, planned remediation, and target completion date
- Prioritize POA&M by risk and Kill Chain phase
- Review and update POA&M at least monthly
- Ensure all POA&M items have realistic target dates before C3PAO assessment

**5c - Gap Assessment**
- Conduct a formal gap assessment against all 287 NIST 800-171A R3 Assessment Objectives
- Score each AO as: Met, Partially Met, Not Met, or Not Applicable
- Identify root cause for each gap (policy missing, tool missing, process missing, training missing)
- Feed all gaps into the POA&M
- Use gap results to prioritize Kill Chain phases 7-22

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] SSP draft complete covering all 97 core controls
- [ ] All 287 Assessment Objectives addressed in SSP
- [ ] POA&M populated with all identified gaps
- [ ] Gap assessment complete with AO-level scoring
- [ ] SSP and POA&M in version-controlled repository
- [ ] Executive sign-off on SSP

---

### NIST 800-171 R3 Controls Addressed
03.12.01-03.12.04 (Security Assessment), 03.16.01-03.16.02 (Planning)

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 5 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 6: Identify Compliance Stakeholders
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 6: Identify Compliance Stakeholders

Compliance is a team sport. This phase ensures every person who touches a NIST 800-171 R3 control knows their role, understands their responsibilities, and has documented procedures to follow.

---

### Sub-components

**6a - RASCI Matrix**
- Build a Responsible, Accountable, Supporting, Consulted, Informed (RASCI) matrix
- Map every NIST 800-171 R3 control to specific individuals or roles
- Ensure no control is unowned
- Identify gaps where no qualified owner exists (triggers a hiring or training need)
- Review RASCI with executive leadership for sign-off

**6b - HR Integration**
- Integrate personnel security requirements into HR operations
- Establish background check requirements for CUI-handling roles
- Define onboarding and offboarding procedures for CUI system access
- Ensure termination procedures trigger account disabling within 24 hours (per DoD ODP 03.01.01.g.02)
- Document separation of duties requirements in job descriptions
- Address NIST 800-171 R3 03.01.04 (Separation of Duties) in HR policy

**6c - Procedures for CUI Handling**
- Develop step-by-step procedures for each CUI-handling process identified in Phase 1
- Procedures must operationalize the policies created in Phase 2
- Cover: creation, labeling, storage, transmission, destruction, and incident reporting of CUI
- Ensure procedures address all 8 undocumented dependency areas from NIST 800-171A R3:
  - Maintenance Operations
  - Roles and Responsibilities
  - Documenting CUI Flow
  - Logical Access Control / Account Management
  - Situational Awareness
  - Comprehensive Inventories
  - Incident Response
  - Physical Security

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] RASCI matrix complete; every control has an assigned owner
- [ ] HR integration documented; onboarding/offboarding procedures updated
- [ ] CUI handling procedures written and published for all relevant roles
- [ ] Separation of duties enforced and documented
- [ ] All 8 undocumented dependency areas addressed in procedures

---

### NIST 800-171 R3 Controls Addressed
03.01.04 (Separation of Duties), 03.01.22 (Publicly Accessible Content), 03.09.01-03.09.02 (Personnel Security)

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 6 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 7: Data Protection Practices
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 7: Data Protection Practices

Develop and implement data protection practices to limit logical and physical access to CUI and/or FCI. POA&M deficiencies to prioritize, resource, and remediate.

---

### Implementation Tasks

- Implement data classification and labeling for all CUI
- Enforce CUI handling requirements at rest, in transit, and in use
- Implement configuration change control (CCB process) per 03.04.03
- Apply least privilege to CUI data stores
- Implement data loss prevention (DLP) controls where applicable
- Ensure media sanitization procedures are documented and enforced
- Protect portable storage devices containing CUI
- Implement controls for CUI on mobile devices

---

### Key NIST 800-171 R3 Controls
03.04.03 (Configuration Change Control), 03.08.01-03.08.09 (Media Protection), 03.13.01 (System and Communications Protection)

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Data classification scheme implemented and enforced
- [ ] CUI labeled and tracked throughout its lifecycle
- [ ] Change Control Board (CCB) process operational
- [ ] Media protection procedures documented and tested
- [ ] Mobile device CUI encryption enforced
- [ ] POA&M items for data protection gaps created and resourced

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 7 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 8: Segmented Network Architecture
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 8: Segmented Network Architecture

Implement a network architecture built on secure engineering principles and enclaves to protect FCI/CUI. POA&M deficiencies to prioritize, resource, and remediate.

---

### Implementation Tasks

- Implement network segmentation between CUI environment and general corporate network
- Create enclaves for CUI processing; enforce information flow controls (03.01.03)
- Deploy firewall rules restricting CUI data flows to authorized paths only
- Remove publicly accessible CUI from public-facing systems (03.01.22.b)
- Implement VPN or equivalent for remote access to CUI systems (03.01.12)
- Enforce wireless access controls (03.01.16)
- Control mobile device connections to CUI network (03.01.18)
- Document and enforce use of external systems (03.01.20)
- Implement network access control (NAC) to enforce device compliance before connection

---

### Key NIST 800-171 R3 Controls
03.01.03 (Information Flow Enforcement), 03.01.12 (Remote Access), 03.01.16 (Wireless Access), 03.01.18 (Mobile Devices), 03.01.20 (External Systems), 03.01.22 (Publicly Accessible Content), 03.13.01-03.13.11 (System and Communications Protection)

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Network segmentation implemented; CUI enclave isolated
- [ ] Information flow enforcement rules documented and configured
- [ ] Remote access routed through controlled access points
- [ ] Wireless access controls configured and enforced
- [ ] External system use policy enforced technically
- [ ] Network diagram updated to reflect current segmented architecture
- [ ] POA&M items for network gaps created

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 8 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 9: Change Management (CM)
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 9: Change Management (CM)

Develop and implement Change Management (CM) practices, including a Change Control Board (CCB). POA&M deficiencies to prioritize, resource, and remediate.

---

### Implementation Tasks

- Establish formal Change Control Board (CCB) with defined membership and authority
- Define categories of configuration-controlled changes (03.04.03.a)
- Implement review and approval process for all changes to CUI systems
- Document all approved changes including security impact analysis
- Implement activity monitoring for configuration-controlled changes
- Maintain current baseline configuration under configuration control (03.04.01)
- Establish configuration settings that reflect most restrictive mode (03.04.02)
- Document and approve any deviations from established configuration settings
- Implement automated configuration management tooling where possible

---

### Key NIST 800-171 R3 Controls
03.04.01 (Baseline Configuration), 03.04.02 (Configuration Settings), 03.04.03 (Configuration Change Control), 03.04.04 (Impact Analyses), 03.04.05 (Access Restrictions for Change), 03.04.06 (Least Functionality), 03.04.07 (Nonlocal Maintenance)

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CCB established with charter and meeting cadence
- [ ] Change management process documented and enforced
- [ ] Baseline configurations documented for all CUI system types
- [ ] Change log maintained and auditable
- [ ] Configuration management tool deployed (e.g., SCCM, Ansible, Chef)
- [ ] Security impact analysis performed for all changes

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 9 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 10: Incident Response (IR)
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 10: Incident Response (IR)

Develop and implement Incident Response (IR) capabilities to detect, respond, and recover from incidents. POA&M deficiencies to prioritize, resource, and remediate.

---

### Implementation Tasks

- Develop a formal Incident Response Plan (IRP)
- Define incident classification and severity levels
- Establish incident reporting procedures (DoD ODP: notification within 72 hours for CUI incidents)
- Designate IR roles: Incident Commander, Analyst, Communications Lead
- Implement incident tracking system (ticketing/case management)
- Establish relationships with US-CERT / DIBNet for CUI incident reporting
- Conduct tabletop exercises (required before D-30)
- Document post-incident analysis and lessons learned process
- Test IR plan at least annually
- Ensure IR covers insider threat scenarios

---

### Key NIST 800-171 R3 Controls
03.06.01-03.06.03 (Incident Response)

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Incident Response Plan (IRP) documented and approved
- [ ] IR roles and responsibilities assigned
- [ ] Incident reporting procedures align with DoD notification requirements
- [ ] DIBNet account established for US-CERT reporting
- [ ] Tabletop exercise completed and documented (required by D-30)
- [ ] IR plan tested; after-action report documented

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 10 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 11: Situational Awareness (SA)
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 11: Situational Awareness (SA)

Develop and implement Situational Awareness (SA) capabilities through threat intelligence, log collection, and analysis (e.g., SIEM, XDR). POA&M deficiencies to prioritize, resource, and remediate.

---

### Implementation Tasks

**Audit Logging (03.03.01-03.03.08)**
- Define event types to log (DoD ODP 03.03.01.a specifies minimum events: authentication, file/object access, privilege use, policy changes, account changes)
- Deploy centralized log collection (SIEM or equivalent)
- Ensure audit records include: event type, timestamp, location, source, outcome, identity (03.03.02)
- Generate audit records for all required event types (03.03.03)
- Retain logs per records retention policy
- Alert on audit logging process failures within defined time period (03.03.04)
- Implement automated log review and analysis
- Preserve log integrity; restrict log management to privileged subset (03.03.08)

**Threat Intelligence**
- Subscribe to DIBNet threat intelligence feeds
- Integrate CISA threat intelligence where applicable
- Correlate threat intelligence with audit log data

---

### Key NIST 800-171 R3 Controls
03.03.01-03.03.08 (Audit and Accountability)

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] SIEM or centralized logging deployed and collecting from all CUI systems
- [ ] Minimum required event types logged per DoD ODP
- [ ] Log integrity protection implemented
- [ ] Automated alerting on log failures configured
- [ ] Log review process documented and operational
- [ ] Threat intelligence feeds integrated

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 11 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 12: Secure Baseline Configurations (SBC)
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 12: Secure Baseline Configurations (SBC)

Develop and implement Secure Baseline Configurations (SBC) - hardening standards - for all technology platforms (servers, workstations, network gear, applications, databases). POA&M deficiencies to prioritize, resource, and remediate.

---

### Implementation Tasks

- Develop hardening standards for each technology platform type in scope
  - Windows Server, Windows Workstation
  - Linux servers
  - Network devices (firewalls, switches, routers)
  - Cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, GCP)
  - Applications and databases
- Reference CIS Benchmarks or DISA STIGs as baseline hardening sources
- Implement account lockout after 5 failed attempts within 5-minute window (DoD ODP 03.01.08)
- Configure device lock after 15 minutes of inactivity (DoD ODP 03.01.10.a)
- Session termination after 24 hours of inactivity maximum (DoD ODP 03.01.11)
- Display system use notification banner before login (03.01.09)
- Implement configuration assessment tool (e.g., Nessus, Qualys, CIS-CAT)
- Automate baseline compliance checking

---

### Key NIST 800-171 R3 Controls
03.01.08 (Unsuccessful Logon Attempts), 03.01.09 (System Use Notification), 03.01.10 (Device Lock), 03.01.11 (Session Termination), 03.04.01 (Baseline Configuration), 03.04.02 (Configuration Settings), 03.04.06 (Least Functionality)

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Hardening standards documented for all platform types
- [ ] Baseline configurations deployed to all in-scope systems
- [ ] Account lockout configured per DoD ODP (5 attempts / 5 minutes)
- [ ] Device lock configured per DoD ODP (15-minute timeout)
- [ ] Session termination configured (24-hour max)
- [ ] System use notification banner deployed
- [ ] Automated compliance scanning operational

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 12 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 13: Identity & Access Management (IAM)
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 13: Identity & Access Management (IAM)

Develop and implement Identity & Access Management (IAM) capabilities to address 'least privilege' and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). POA&M deficiencies to prioritize, resource, and remediate.

---

### Implementation Tasks

**Account Management (03.01.01)**
- Define allowed account types (user, service, admin, shared)
- Implement automated account provisioning and de-provisioning
- Disable accounts inactive for 90 days maximum (DoD ODP 03.01.01.f.02)
- Notify account managers within 24 hours of termination/transfer (DoD ODP 03.01.01.g.01-.03)
- Require logout after 24-hour inactivity or at work period end for privileged users (DoD ODP 03.01.01.h)
- Monitor account usage continuously

**Least Privilege (03.01.05)**
- Implement RBAC aligned to job functions
- Review privileges at least every 12 months (DoD ODP 03.01.05.c)
- Authorize specific security functions to defined roles (DoD ODP 03.01.05.b)
- Restrict privileged accounts to only defined administrative roles (DoD ODP 03.01.06.a)
- Require privileged users to use non-privileged accounts for non-security functions
- Prevent non-privileged users from executing privileged functions; log all privileged function execution

**Access Enforcement (03.01.02)**
- Enforce approved access authorizations to CUI and system resources
- Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all CUI system access
- Implement privileged access workstations (PAWs) for admin functions where feasible

---

### Key NIST 800-171 R3 Controls
03.01.01 (Account Management), 03.01.02 (Access Enforcement), 03.01.05 (Least Privilege), 03.01.06 (Least Privilege - Privileged Accounts), 03.01.07 (Least Privilege - Privileged Functions), 03.05.01-03.05.11 (Identification and Authentication)

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] RBAC implemented for all CUI systems
- [ ] Account inactivity policy enforced (90-day disable)
- [ ] Termination-triggered account disable within 24 hours
- [ ] Least privilege reviews scheduled and documented
- [ ] Privileged account restrictions enforced technically
- [ ] MFA deployed for all CUI system access
- [ ] Privileged function execution logged

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 13 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 14: Proactive Maintenance
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 14: Proactive Maintenance

Develop and implement proactive maintenance practices. POA&M deficiencies to prioritize, resource, and remediate.

---

### Implementation Tasks

- Develop a maintenance policy covering all in-scope systems
- Schedule and document regular preventive maintenance activities
- Implement controls for maintenance activities that require CUI system access
- Restrict system maintenance to authorized personnel
- Require MFA or equivalent for remote maintenance sessions
- Sanitize equipment prior to removal from CUI environment for maintenance
- Inspect maintenance equipment for unauthorized modifications
- Document all maintenance activities in a maintenance log
- Control use of maintenance tools

---

### Key NIST 800-171 R3 Controls
03.07.01-03.07.06 (Maintenance)

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Maintenance policy documented
- [ ] Maintenance schedule established for all CUI systems
- [ ] Remote maintenance sessions require MFA and are logged
- [ ] Maintenance authorization process documented
- [ ] Maintenance log operational
- [ ] Equipment sanitization procedure before external maintenance

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 14 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 15: Attack Surface Management (ASM)
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 15: Attack Surface Management (ASM)

Develop and implement Attack Surface Management (ASM) practices to identify and remediate vulnerabilities. POA&M deficiencies to prioritize, resource, and remediate.

---

### Implementation Tasks

- Implement vulnerability scanning at minimum quarterly cadence (DoD ODP requirement)
- Conduct authenticated scans of all in-scope systems
- Scan for both known vulnerabilities (CVEs) and misconfigurations
- Establish vulnerability remediation SLAs:
  - Critical: 15 days
  - High: 30 days
  - Medium: 90 days
  - Low: 180 days (or documented risk acceptance)
- Feed unresolved vulnerabilities into POA&M
- Monitor for newly published vulnerabilities affecting in-scope systems (threat intel integration)
- Conduct penetration testing prior to C3PAO assessment
- Implement patch management process tied to vulnerability scanning results
- Track external attack surface (internet-facing assets)

---

### Key NIST 800-171 R3 Controls
03.11.02-03.11.03 (Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning), 03.14.01-03.14.02 (Flaw Remediation)

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Vulnerability scanner deployed and scanning all CUI systems
- [ ] Quarterly scan schedule established
- [ ] Remediation SLAs defined and enforced
- [ ] Vulnerability findings linked to POA&M
- [ ] Penetration test completed prior to D-90
- [ ] Patch management process documented and operational

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 15 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 16: IT Asset Management (ITAM)
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 16: IT Asset Management (ITAM)

Develop and implement IT Asset Management (ITAM) practices. POA&M deficiencies to prioritize, resource, and remediate.

---

### Implementation Tasks

- Implement a comprehensive hardware and software asset inventory system
- Ensure all CUI system assets are tagged and tracked
- Implement controls for external system use (03.01.20)
- Prohibit use of unauthorized external systems
- Establish security requirements for external systems before allowing access
- Restrict portable storage device use on external systems
- Track software licenses and versions
- Implement CMDB (Configuration Management Database) or equivalent
- Conduct periodic asset inventory reconciliation
- Track End-of-Life (EOL) software and hardware; plan replacements

---

### Key NIST 800-171 R3 Controls
03.01.20 (Use of External Systems), 03.04.01 (Baseline Configuration - asset tracking component)

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] ITAM system deployed and tracking all CUI-environment assets
- [ ] Hardware inventory complete and reconciled with Phase 3 asset inventory
- [ ] Software inventory complete; unauthorized software controls in place
- [ ] External system use policy enforced
- [ ] Portable storage device controls implemented
- [ ] EOL tracking established with replacement plans documented

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 16 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 17: Layered Network Defenses
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 17: Layered Network Defenses

Develop and implement layered network security for Defense-in-Depth (DiD) practices. POA&M deficiencies to prioritize, resource, and remediate.

---

### Implementation Tasks

- Implement Defense-in-Depth (DiD) architecture with multiple security layers
- Deploy next-generation firewall (NGFW) at network perimeter
- Implement intrusion detection/prevention system (IDS/IPS)
- Deploy endpoint detection and response (EDR/XDR)
- Configure remote access controls: usage restrictions, configuration requirements, connection requirements (03.01.12)
- Route all remote access through authorized access control points
- Control wireless access: encryption, authentication, disable when not in use (03.01.16)
- Implement mobile device management (MDM) for CUI-capable mobile devices (03.01.18)
- Deploy email security (anti-phishing, anti-spam, DKIM/SPF/DMARC)
- Implement DNS security filtering
- Monitor network traffic for anomalies

---

### Key NIST 800-171 R3 Controls
03.01.12 (Remote Access), 03.01.16 (Wireless Access), 03.01.18 (Mobile Devices), 03.13.01-03.13.11 (System and Communications Protection)

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] NGFW deployed and configured at all CUI network boundaries
- [ ] IDS/IPS operational and alerting
- [ ] EDR deployed to all CUI endpoints
- [ ] Remote access routing enforced through controlled points
- [ ] Wireless access encryption (WPA3 or equivalent) deployed
- [ ] MDM deployed for all CUI-capable mobile devices
- [ ] Email security controls implemented

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 17 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 18: Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery (BC/DR)
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 18: Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery (BC/DR)

Develop and implement Business Continuity / Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) capabilities. POA&M deficiencies to prioritize, resource, and remediate.

---

### Implementation Tasks

- Develop a Business Continuity Plan (BCP)
- Develop a Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP)
- Define Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) for all CUI systems
- Implement backup procedures that protect CUI integrity
- Store backups in a geographically separate and secure location
- Test backup restoration at least annually
- Conduct BC/DR tabletop exercise (required by D-30)
- Ensure BC/DR plans address CUI protection during disruption
- Document alternate processing sites for critical CUI systems
- Establish communication plan for disruption scenarios

---

### Key NIST 800-171 R3 Controls
03.06.02 (Incident Response Testing), 03.08.09 (Backup - media protection)

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] BCP documented and approved
- [ ] DRP documented and approved
- [ ] RTO/RPO defined for all CUI systems
- [ ] Backup procedures implemented; restoration tested
- [ ] BC/DR tabletop exercise conducted and documented (by D-30)
- [ ] Alternate processing site identified and validated

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 18 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 19: Cryptographic Key Management
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 19: Cryptographic Key Management

Develop and implement cryptographic key management and data encryption capabilities. POA&M deficiencies to prioritize, resource, and remediate.

---

### Implementation Tasks

- Implement FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated cryptographic modules for all CUI encryption
- Encrypt CUI at rest on all storage systems (workstations, servers, mobile devices, removable media)
- Encrypt CUI in transit using TLS 1.2 minimum (TLS 1.3 preferred)
- Develop cryptographic key management procedures:
  - Key generation, distribution, storage, rotation, revocation, and destruction
- Implement a key management system (KMS) or HSM for enterprise key management
- Establish key rotation schedules
- Protect private keys with access controls
- Ensure cloud-provider encryption uses customer-managed keys (CMKs) where possible
- Prohibit use of non-FIPS-validated encryption for CUI

---

### Key NIST 800-171 R3 Controls
03.13.08 (Cryptographic Protection), 03.13.10 (Cryptographic Key Establishment and Management)

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated modules in use for all CUI encryption
- [ ] Full-disk encryption deployed to all CUI endpoints
- [ ] CUI in transit encrypted with TLS 1.2+
- [ ] Key management procedures documented
- [ ] KMS or HSM deployed for enterprise key management
- [ ] Key rotation schedule established and automated where possible

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 19 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 20: Physical Security
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 20: Physical Security

Develop and implement physical security practices. POA&M deficiencies and document procedures.

---

### Implementation Tasks

- Define physical access boundaries for CUI processing areas
- Implement access control to CUI facilities (badge readers, locks, guards)
- Maintain access logs for CUI areas; review regularly
- Control visitor access: escorting, logging, badges
- Implement surveillance (cameras) for CUI areas where appropriate
- Protect CUI systems from physical tampering
- Implement clean desk / clear screen policy
- Control physical media containing CUI (storage, transport, destruction)
- Ensure data center / server room physical security meets requirements
- Address physical security in PPTDF documentation (Facilities component)

**Note:** Physical Security is one of the 8 undocumented dependency areas identified in NIST 800-171A R3 - many organizations overlook the procedural documentation requirements.

---

### Key NIST 800-171 R3 Controls
03.10.01-03.10.06 (Physical Protection)

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Physical access control implemented for all CUI areas
- [ ] Visitor access procedures documented and enforced
- [ ] Physical access logs maintained and reviewed
- [ ] Surveillance implemented where required
- [ ] Clean desk / clear screen policy published and enforced
- [ ] Physical security procedures documented (addressing undocumented dependency)

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 20 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 21: Security Awareness Training
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 21: Security Awareness Training

Develop and implement training & awareness to ensure a security-minded workforce. POA&M deficiencies to prioritize, resource, and remediate.

---

### Implementation Tasks

**General Security Awareness (03.02.01)**
- Provide security literacy training to all users at least annually (DoD ODP 03.02.01.a.01)
- Conduct training after significant security events or risk changes (DoD ODP 03.02.01.a.02)
- Include training on: insider threat recognition, social engineering, social mining, phishing
- Update training content at least annually (DoD ODP 03.02.01.b.01)

**Role-Based Training (03.02.02)**
- Provide role-based training before CUI system access is granted
- Conduct role-based training at least annually thereafter (DoD ODP 03.02.02.a.01)
- Update role-based content at least annually (DoD ODP 03.02.02.b.01)
- Cover roles: system administrators, security personnel, CUI handlers, executives

**Training Program**
- Implement a training platform that tracks completion and generates reports
- Include phishing simulation exercises
- Document training records for all personnel
- Ensure training addresses CUI handling requirements specific to the organization

---

### Key NIST 800-171 R3 Controls
03.02.01 (Literacy Training and Awareness), 03.02.02 (Role-Based Training)

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Security awareness training program implemented
- [ ] All personnel completed initial training before CUI system access
- [ ] Annual refresher training scheduled
- [ ] Role-based training defined for all CUI-handling roles
- [ ] Training records maintained; completion tracked
- [ ] Phishing simulation program operational
- [ ] Training content updated after DoD ODP-defined trigger events

---

### Reference
Kill Chain Phase 21 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: Phase 22: Internal Audit (IA)
issues.body:
## Kill Chain Phase 22: Internal Audit (IA)

Develop and implement an 'internal audit' or Information Assurance (IA) capability to govern controls. POA&M deficiencies to prioritize, resource, and remediate.

---

### Implementation Tasks

- Establish an internal audit program for NIST 800-171 R3 compliance
- Define audit scope, frequency, and methodology
- Conduct internal audits against all 97 core CUI controls (AO level)
- Ensure auditors are independent from the functions being audited
- Document audit findings; link to POA&M for remediation tracking
- Conduct continuous monitoring of control effectiveness
- Implement a formal corrective action process for audit findings
- Prepare for external assessment by conducting a mock C3PAO assessment
- Maintain audit records and evidence library
- Define criteria for escalating findings to executive leadership

**Pre-Assessment Internal Audit Checklist:**
- [ ] All Phase 1-21 deliverables complete
- [ ] SSP current and approved
- [ ] POA&M up-to-date with all known gaps
- [ ] Evidence library organized for C3PAO review
- [ ] Change freeze in place (D-45)
- [ ] IR tabletop complete (D-30)
- [ ] No open Critical or High vulnerabilities without accepted risk
- [ ] All personnel training complete

---

### Key NIST 800-171 R3 Controls
03.12.01-03.12.04 (Security Assessment and Monitoring)

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Internal audit program established with charter
- [ ] Annual internal audit scheduled and conducted
- [ ] Mock C3PAO assessment completed before D-45
- [ ] All audit findings entered in POA&M
- [ ] Corrective action process operational
- [ ] Evidence library organized for C3PAO

---

Kill Chain Phase 22 | ComplianceForge NIST 800-171 R3 Kill Chain (2024.2)

issues.title: R2 to R3 Overview: Understanding the Scope of Change
issues.body:
## R2 to R3 Transition: Overview

This project tracks the AO-level transition from NIST 800-171 R2 to NIST 800-171 R3. Understanding the full scope of change is required before allocating resources.

---

### Key Statistics

| Metric | NIST 800-171 R2 | NIST 800-171 R3 |
|--------|----------------|----------------|
| CUI Controls | 110 | 97 (core) / 287 (discrete requirements) |
| NFO Controls | 61 | 0 (incorporated into CUI controls) |
| Assessment Objectives (AOs) | 320 | 510 |
| AO Change | - | +59% increase |

### AO Transition Breakdown

| Transition Type | Count | % | Effort Level |
|----------------|-------|---|-------------|
| Direct mapping from R2 | 171 | 34% | Minimal |
| Indirect mapping from R2 | 110 | 22% | Moderate |
| No clear R2 mapping | 57 | 11% | Significant |
| New for R3 (no R2 path) | 172 | 34% | Significant |
| **Total R3 AOs** | **510** | **100%** | - |

---

### Tasks for This Issue

- [ ] Brief executive leadership on scope of R2-to-R3 change
- [ ] Obtain executive approval and budget for transition project
- [ ] Assign a Transition Project Manager
- [ ] Schedule AO-level gap assessment against all 510 R3 AOs
- [ ] Document all 510 R3 AOs in SSP (complete, partial, or POA&M)
- [ ] Establish transition project timeline

---

### Source
NIST 800-171 R2 to R3 Transition Guide (2026.1) - Tom Cornelius (ComplianceForge) and Ryan Bonner (DEFCERT)

issues.title: DoD Organization Defined Parameters (ODPs) - Implement All 34 DoD-Specified Values
issues.body:
## DoD Organization Defined Parameters (ODPs)

On April 10, 2025, the DoD CIO released a memorandum specifying minimum criteria for NIST SP 800-171 R3 Organizational Defined Parameters (ODPs). All 34 DoD-specified ODPs must be implemented and documented in policy and/or SSP.

---

### Complete DoD ODP Table

| Control ID | ODP Description | DoD-Specified Value |
|-----------|----------------|--------------------|
| 03.01.01.f.02 | Account inactivity threshold | At most 90 days |
| 03.01.01.g.01 | Notify when account no longer required | 24 hours |
| 03.01.01.g.02 | Notify when user terminated | 24 hours |
| 03.01.01.g.03 | Notify when need-to-know changes | 24 hours |
| 03.01.01.h.01 | Inactivity logout period | At most 24 hours |
| 03.01.01.h.02 | Circumstances requiring logout | At work period end (privileged users minimum) |
| 03.01.05.b.01 | Authorized security functions | Defined list including account mgmt, privilege config, audit settings, vuln scanning, IDS parameters, audit info mgmt |
| 03.01.05.b.02 | Security-relevant information | Defined list including threat/vuln info, firewall rules, config params, crypto key info, ACLs, audit info |
| 03.01.05.c | Privilege review frequency | At least every 12 months |
| 03.01.06.a | Privileged account restriction | Only defined and authorized personnel or administrative roles |
| 03.01.08.a.01 | Max failed logon attempts | At most five (5) |
| 03.01.08.a.02 | Failed logon time window | Period of five (5) minutes |
| 03.01.08.b | Post-lockout action | Lock account 15+ minutes OR lock until admin release AND notify admin |
| 03.01.10.a | Device lock inactivity trigger | At most 15 minutes |
| 03.01.11 | Session termination conditions | Max 24-hour inactivity; misbehavior; maintenance |
| 03.02.01.a.01 | Security literacy training frequency | At least every 12 months |
| 03.02.01.a.02 | Training trigger events | Significant/novel incidents or significant risk changes |
| 03.02.01.b.01 | Training content update frequency | At least every 12 months |
| 03.02.01.b.02 | Training content trigger events | Significant/novel incidents or significant risk changes |
| 03.02.02.a.01 | Role-based training frequency | At least every 12 months |
| 03.02.02.a.02 | Role-based trigger events | Significant/novel incidents or significant risk changes |
| 03.02.02.b.01 | Role-based content update frequency | At least every 12 months |
| 03.02.02.b.02 | Role-based content trigger events | Significant/novel incidents or significant risk changes |
| 03.03.01.a | Event types for logging | Min: Authentication (logon/logoff), File/Object (create/access/delete/modify/permission), Account changes, Privilege use, Policy changes, System events |
| 03.04.02.a | Configuration settings | Most restrictive mode consistent with operations |

*(Additional ODPs covering password length [16-char minimum per DoD guidance], vulnerability scanning frequency [quarterly], and others are documented in the Transition Guide.)*

---

### Implementation Checklist

- [ ] All 34 ODPs documented in Information Security Policy or Standards
- [ ] Account inactivity policy (90-day) implemented technically
- [ ] Account notification (24-hour) implemented in HR process and technically
- [ ] Failed logon lockout (5 attempts / 5 min / 15-min lock) configured
- [ ] Device lock (15-minute timeout) configured on all CUI endpoints
- [ ] Session termination (24-hour max) configured
- [ ] Training frequency (annual + trigger-based) scheduled
- [ ] Privilege review (annual) scheduled
- [ ] Logging event types meeting DoD minimum list
- [ ] SSP updated to reference all ODP values

---

### Source
NIST 800-171 R2 to R3 Transition Guide (2026.1) - DoD CIO Memorandum, April 10, 2025

issues.title: Undocumented Dependencies: Address All 8 Areas
issues.body:
## Undocumented Dependencies in NIST 800-171A R3

NIST 800-171A R3 has 8 dependency areas that are not explicitly called out as standalone controls but are implicitly required by the AOs. Organizations that fail to address these dependencies will have gaps that assessors will flag.

---

### The 8 Undocumented Dependency Areas

**1. Maintenance Operations**
- R3 AOs reference maintenance activities but do not have a dedicated 'document your maintenance process' control
- Action: Document all system maintenance procedures, including authorization, scheduling, remote maintenance controls, equipment handling, and post-maintenance verification

**2. Roles and Responsibilities**
- Multiple R3 AOs reference 'organizational personnel or roles' without specifying where those roles must be defined
- Action: Maintain a current RASCI matrix; ensure every control references specific named roles; update job descriptions to reflect security responsibilities

**3. Documenting the Flow of CUI**
- Data flow documentation is implicitly required by numerous AOs (information flow enforcement, access control, media protection) but no single control mandates a DFD
- Action: Maintain a current Data Flow Diagram (DFD) showing all CUI creation, processing, storage, transmission, and destruction points

**4. Logical Access Control / Account Management**
- The volume of access control AOs in R3 creates implicit dependency on a mature account management process
- Action: Implement a formal access control procedure covering: provisioning, modification, periodic review, termination, emergency access, and privileged access; document the process and enforce technically

**5. Situational Awareness**
- Audit logging AOs (03.03.x) collectively require a logging strategy that is not explicitly mandated as a single document
- Action: Document a Logging and Monitoring Strategy covering: what is logged, where logs are stored, who reviews them, how long they are retained, and how alerting works

**6. Comprehensive Inventories**
- Asset management AOs reference inventories but R3 does not mandate a formal inventory standard
- Action: Maintain current, comprehensive inventories of hardware, software, external service providers, and users with CUI access; reconcile at defined frequency

**7. Incident Response**
- IR AOs (03.06.x) are fewer than expected, but assessors will look for evidence of a complete IR program (plan, procedures, training, testing, post-incident analysis)
- Action: Ensure IRP covers the full IR lifecycle; document tabletop exercises; maintain IR records; address insider threat in IR procedures

**8. Physical Security**
- Physical protection AOs (03.10.x) require documented procedures that many organizations have only as informal practices
- Action: Document physical security procedures for: facility access, visitor management, equipment handling, media protection in physical spaces, and environmental controls

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Maintenance Operations procedures documented
- [ ] RASCI matrix current and covers all R3 controls
- [ ] Current DFD maintained and accessible in SSP
- [ ] Access management procedure documented and enforced
- [ ] Logging and Monitoring Strategy documented
- [ ] All inventory types (HW, SW, ESP, users) maintained and current
- [ ] IRP covers full lifecycle including physical security and insider threat
- [ ] Physical security procedures documented

---

### Source
NIST 800-171 R2 to R3 Transition Guide (2026.1) - Section: Undocumented Dependencies

issues.title: Minimal Effort AOs: Verify 171 Direct-Mapped AOs Are Current
issues.body:
## Minimal Effort AO Transition (171 AOs - 34% of R3 Total)

These 171 R3 Assessment Objectives directly map to existing NIST 800-171 R2 AOs. Organizations that were compliant with R2 for these controls should require minimal effort - primarily verification and documentation updates.

---

### What 'Minimal Effort' Means

Direct mapping means:
- The R3 AO language is substantially the same as or narrower than the R2 AO
- Evidence from R2 compliance is likely still valid
- Primary task is verification that controls remain implemented and documentation is current in the R3 SSP format

### What To Do

1. Review each of the 171 direct-mapped AOs in the Transition Guide
2. Verify the control is still implemented as documented
3. Update SSP language to use R3 control numbering and terminology
4. Confirm DoD ODP values are incorporated where applicable
5. Add to POA&M if control implementation has lapsed

---

### Control Families Covered (direct mappings)
Access Control (AC), Audit and Accountability (AU), Configuration Management (CM), Identification and Authentication (IA), Incident Response (IR), Maintenance (MA), Media Protection (MP), Personnel Security (PS), Physical Protection (PE), Risk Assessment (RA), System and Communications Protection (SC), System and Information Integrity (SI)

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 171 direct-mapped AOs reviewed against current implementation
- [ ] SSP updated with R3 control numbers for all 171 AOs
- [ ] Gaps from R2 compliance identified and added to POA&M
- [ ] DoD ODP values verified for applicable direct-mapped AOs

---

### Source
NIST 800-171 R2 to R3 Transition Guide (2026.1) - Section: Minimal Effort Assessment Objective Transition

issues.title: Moderate Effort AOs: Remediate 110 Indirect-Mapped AOs
issues.body:
## Moderate Effort AO Transition (110 AOs - 22% of R3 Total)

These 110 R3 Assessment Objectives indirectly map to R2 AOs. They cover similar territory but with expanded or modified requirements. Existing R2 controls provide a foundation but will need updating to fully meet R3 requirements.

---

### What 'Moderate Effort' Means

Indirect mapping means:
- The R3 AO is related to an R2 AO but broader, more specific, or reframed
- Existing evidence is partially applicable but may contain assumptions that no longer hold
- Work required: close gaps between what R2 required and what R3 actually requires
- Documentation may need significant rewriting to align with R3 language

### What To Do

1. Review each of the 110 indirect-mapped AOs against current R2 implementation
2. Identify the specific delta between R2 and R3 requirements
3. Remediate gaps (policy, process, or technical controls)
4. Update SSP to reflect R3-compliant implementation
5. Gather new evidence where R2 evidence is insufficient
6. Update POA&M for gaps that cannot be remediated immediately

---

### Common Themes in Indirect Mappings
- R3 often adds specificity (e.g., 'within 24 hours' where R2 said 'timely')
- R3 sometimes splits one R2 AO into multiple discrete sub-AOs
- NFO controls from R2 have been incorporated into CUI controls in R3 with additional requirements
- DoD ODPs add specific values to previously open-ended R2 requirements

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 110 indirect-mapped AOs reviewed and delta documented
- [ ] Gaps remediated or entered in POA&M
- [ ] SSP updated with R3-compliant implementation descriptions
- [ ] New evidence gathered for AOs where R2 evidence is insufficient

---

### Source
NIST 800-171 R2 to R3 Transition Guide (2026.1) - Section: Moderate Effort Assessment Objective Transition

issues.title: Significant Effort AOs: Implement 57 AOs with No Clear R2 Mapping
issues.body:
## Significant Effort AO Transition (57 AOs - 11% of R3 Total)

These 57 R3 Assessment Objectives have no clear mapping to any R2 AO. They represent requirements that were either not addressed by R2 or have been substantially restructured. Full implementation from scratch is required.

---

### What 'Significant Effort - No Clear Mapping' Means

- No R2 AO directly addresses these requirements
- Organizations cannot rely on existing R2 compliance
- May require new policies, processes, tools, or technical controls
- Some of these address areas that R2 treated informally or left to organization discretion

### What To Do

1. Review each of the 57 AOs with no R2 mapping
2. Assess current state: is anything in place that partially addresses the requirement?
3. Design and implement new controls from the ground up
4. Document in SSP with new implementation descriptions
5. Enter in POA&M with realistic remediation timelines
6. Prioritize by risk and C3PAO assessment timeline

---

### Key Areas Covered by No-Mapping AOs
These AOs tend to cluster around: advanced configuration management requirements, supply chain risk management specifics, enhanced access control sub-controls, and new system and communications protection requirements.

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 57 no-mapping AOs reviewed and assessed against current state
- [ ] New controls designed and implementation roadmap documented
- [ ] All 57 AOs either implemented or in POA&M with timeline
- [ ] SSP updated

---

### Source
NIST 800-171 R2 to R3 Transition Guide (2026.1) - Section: Significant Effort Assessment Objective Transition

issues.title: New R3 AOs: Implement 172 Controls New to NIST 800-171 R3
issues.body:
## New R3 AOs (172 AOs - 34% of R3 Total)

These 172 Assessment Objectives are completely new to NIST 800-171 R3 - they come from controls that did not exist in R2. This is the largest single category of transition work and represents the 260% increase in discrete requirements.

---

### What 'New for R3' Means

- These AOs originate from controls that were not in NIST 800-171 R2
- There is no R2 evidence to leverage
- Full implementation from scratch is required for all 172 AOs
- Many derive from NFO controls that have been elevated to CUI control status in R3
- Some address entirely new security domains (e.g., enhanced supply chain, advanced authentication)

### What To Do

1. Review all 172 new R3 AOs from the Transition Guide
2. Prioritize by: risk level, Kill Chain phase alignment, and C3PAO assessment timeline
3. Map each new AO to a responsible owner (update RASCI)
4. Design and implement new controls
5. Document all new implementations in SSP
6. Enter all gaps in POA&M

---

### Prioritization Guidance

New AOs that align to Kill Chain Phases 1-6 (governance foundations) should be implemented first. New AOs that align to Phases 7-13 (core technical controls) are second priority. New AOs in Phases 14-22 (advanced program maturity) can follow.

---

### Key Control Families with Significant New AOs
- Access Control (03.01.x) - new sub-controls for account management
- Audit and Accountability (03.03.x) - expanded logging requirements
- Configuration Management (03.04.x) - new CM sub-controls
- Identification and Authentication (03.05.x) - new MFA and authentication requirements
- Risk Assessment (03.11.x) - new supply chain and risk requirements
- System and Communications Protection (03.13.x) - new encryption and network controls

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 172 new R3 AOs reviewed and ownership assigned
- [ ] Prioritized implementation roadmap documented
- [ ] All 172 AOs either implemented or in POA&M with realistic dates
- [ ] SSP updated with new AO implementation descriptions

---

issues.title: Practical Transition Step: Governance Oversight
issues.body:
## Practical Transition Step: Governance Oversight

Before implementing technical controls, governance must be updated to reflect R3 requirements. This is the first of two practical transition steps identified in the Transition Guide.

---

### Assumptions

This step assumes the organization already has:
- A System Security Plan (SSP) from R2
- An existing policy framework
- An External Service Provider (ESP) inventory

If any of these are missing, complete the Kill Chain Phase 1-6 work first.

---

### Key Governance Transition Tasks

**Update Policies and Standards**
- Review all existing information security policies against the 510 R3 AOs
- Update policy language to incorporate R3 requirements and DoD ODP values
- Add new policy sections for R3 control areas not previously covered
- Update the SSP to reflect R3 control numbering and implementation descriptions
- Obtain executive approval for all updated policies

**Inventory External Service Providers (ESPs)**
- Update ESP inventory to reflect current third-party services
- Assess each ESP for CMMC Level 2 / NIST 800-171 R3 compliance
- Obtain compliance evidence from each critical ESP
- For cloud services: confirm FedRAMP authorization or equivalent
- Document ESP assessments in SSP and C-SCRM Plan
- Flow down CMMC requirements to subcontractors handling CUI

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All policies reviewed and updated for R3
- [ ] SSP updated from R2 to R3 control numbering
- [ ] DoD ODP values incorporated into policy language
- [ ] ESP inventory current and compliance status documented for all ESPs
- [ ] CMMC flow-down requirements included in subcontractor agreements
- [ ] Executive sign-off on updated policies

---

### Source

issues.title: Practical Transition Step: Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) Plan
issues.body:
## Practical Transition Step: Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) Plan

NIST 800-171 R3 significantly expands supply chain risk management requirements compared to R2. A formal C-SCRM Plan is now required. This is the second practical transition step identified in the Transition Guide.

---

### Background

NIST 800-171 R3 introduces dedicated Supply Chain Risk Management controls (03.16.03) that require organizations to manage risks from their supply chain - including hardware, software, and services. This was only lightly addressed in R2.

---

### C-SCRM Plan Requirements

**Document the C-SCRM Plan covering:**
- Identification of critical suppliers and third-party components in the CUI supply chain
- Risk assessment process for suppliers (initial and periodic)
- Acquisition security requirements (how you vet new suppliers)
- Counterfeit component controls (especially for hardware)
- Software supply chain security (e.g., SBOMs, provenance verification)
- Incident response procedures specific to supply chain compromises
- Supplier monitoring and ongoing assessment process

**Implementation Actions:**
- Identify all suppliers with access to CUI or CUI systems
- Assess supply chain risk for each critical supplier
- Establish acquisition security requirements embedded in procurement contracts
- Implement CMMC flow-down clauses in subcontractor agreements
- Monitor suppliers for security incidents and compliance changes
- Reference NIST SP 800-161r1 for C-SCRM methodology

---

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] C-SCRM Plan documented and approved
- [ ] All critical suppliers identified and risk-assessed
- [ ] Acquisition security requirements embedded in procurement process
- [ ] CMMC flow-down in all relevant subcontractor agreements
- [ ] Supplier monitoring process operational
- [ ] C-SCRM Plan referenced in SSP

---

### Source
NIST 800-171 R2 to R3 Transition Guide (2026.1) - Section: Practical Steps, Supply Chain Risk Management Plan

issues.title: Orphaned R2 AOs: Track End-of-Life Assessment Objectives
issues.body:
## Orphaned R2 AOs: End-of-Life (EOL) Assessment Objectives

Some NIST 800-171 R2 Assessment Objectives do not carry forward to R3. These 'orphaned' AOs were either withdrawn, incorporated into other controls, or eliminated. Organizations must identify which R2 controls they were relying on that no longer exist in R3, and determine whether the underlying security objective is still addressed elsewhere.

---

### What Orphaned AOs Mean

- The R2 AO has been formally withdrawn or incorporated into another control
- The R2 control number may no longer appear in R3 assessment guides
- If your SSP references these R2 controls, they need to be replaced with the appropriate R3 control reference
- The security objective may still exist but under a different control number

### Examples of Withdrawn R2 Controls in R3
From the mapping table in the Kill Chain document:
- 03.01.13 - Withdrawn (Addressed by 03.13.08)
- 03.01.14 - Withdrawn (Incorporated into 03.01.12)
- 03.01.15 - Withdrawn (Incorporated into 03.01.12)
- 03.01.17 - Withdrawn (Incorporated into 03.01.16)
- 03.01.19 - Withdrawn (Incorporated into 03.01.18)
- 03.01.21 - Withdrawn (Incorporated into 03.01.20)
- 03.02.03 - Withdrawn (Incorporated into 03.02.01)
- 03.03.09 - Withdrawn (Incorporated into 03.03.08)

*(Additional withdrawn controls exist - reference the full Transition Guide for the complete list.)*

---

### Tasks

- [ ] Review all withdrawn/incorporated R2 controls from the Transition Guide
- [ ] Update SSP to remove references to withdrawn control numbers
- [ ] Confirm that security objective of each withdrawn control is addressed by the absorbing R3 control
- [ ] Update any policies or procedures that reference withdrawn control numbers
- [ ] Note that some withdrawn controls may reduce overall AO count but the requirement remains

---
